name: rother_vwap_day_a24

source.title: Ex-Hedge Fund Manager Trades His $150M VWAP Strategy Live (Full Breakdown)

entry.words: Price moves away from VWAP and comes back: put a limit order AT the VWAP and let it fill on the first touch only; if price comes within two or three ticks and pulls back, take the order out (the second or third touch is not A+).

taught: [8:30] if the market is moving away from VWAP and coming back to VWAP we see a reaction: that is what he trades
[9:04-9:39] three VWAPs: the day VWAP from the electronic open (18:00 ET), the London VWAP from the London open, the US session VWAP from regular trading hours
[21:18-22:24] a limit order at the VWAP; the first touch is the A+ setup; if price is two or three ticks from the order and pulls back, the order is taken out
[20:10] stop 10 ticks, target 10 to 15 ticks; win rate said to be 80% at about 1.1 to 1
[31:13] the order sits exactly at VWAP and is moved by hand as VWAP moves
[53:00-54:30] never closes early, never moves the target: 'I never could improve it'
not_run: Day VWAP: the video's day VWAP starts 18:00 ET. The engine's morning instance reads the trade date's bars from 00:00 ET, so the day VWAP here starts at 00:00 ET (the first six evening hours are missing).
London VWAP: no clock time was said; 03:00 ET (08:00 London, 02:00 Central) is my reading.
'Which VWAP is most respected' is a look at the chart with no rule: each VWAP is run alone as its own sheet.
'Away' is not a number in the video: the setting is mine (ticks away from VWAP before a return counts); three values are run as three sheets and none is picked.
Skipping sideways days has no rule and is not run (no filter). The Bookmap liquidity check is not run (he says to skip it: 'just take the trade').
The 'bad feeling' early exit and the swing-low liquidity sweep trade are not run.

The limit order is re-priced at every bar close of the sheet's bar size (1 or 5 minutes), not continuously. A limit fills on a one-tick trade-through (a touch to the tick is no fill): his own fills may be easier.
max_trades 5 a pass is mine (the video gives no cap); sessions are separate passes, so a cap counts inside each pass.
The video's market is ES; costs are the engine's own (1 tick of slippage on market and stop fills, $4 a round turn).
